table.title: தமிழ் / বাংলা · Mixed Indic
table.md:
| மொழி | ভাষা | பேசுவோர் | குறிப்பு |
|---|---|---|---|
| தமிழ் | তামিল | 8 கோடி | உலகின் மிகப் பழமையான செம்மொழிகளில் ஒன்றாகக் கருதப்படுகிறது. |
| বাংলা | বাংলা | 23 கோடி | বিশ্বের সপ্তম বৃহত্তম ভাষা, বাংলাদেশ ও পশ্চিমবঙ্গে প্রচলিত। |
| हिन्दी | হিন্দি | 60 கோடி | — |

understanding.purpose: Compare languages across Tamil and Bengali names, speaker counts, and brief notes.
understanding.reading: Readers scan each row from the two language names to the speaker count and note, and compare counts down the third column.
groups: Columns 1 and 2 give the same language name in two scripts, so they should read as a pair.
Column 3 gives the comparable numeric measure; column 4 provides descriptive context.
keep_intact: Unbreakable words in the notes where space permits
may_wrap: Notes in column 4 can wrap at natural word boundaries; their longer text can determine row height.
Short headers or values can wrap where necessary, with the other cells sharing the resulting row height.

preferred.name: r0A
preferred.note: Keep the longest unbreakable content intact in every column and give the remaining space to the notes.

acceptable.name: r0C
acceptable.note: Give the paired language names comfortable widths and favor the notes over the speaker-count column, accepting a tight third-column header.

bad.name: r0B
bad.note: Give the notes more room by narrowing all three comparison columns, accepting tighter wrapping or overflow for their longest unbreakable content.
bad.why: Two headers wrap and language names split within words, disrupting the first two columns where readers identify each row.

rationale: r0A keeps the headers, language names and speaker counts intact, so readers can scan across each row before turning to the longer notes. Its wider speaker column also keeps the short final row compact. r0C preserves words but wraps the speaker header and counts, weakening that column's scan rhythm.

general: Preserve recognizable words and identifiers, especially in columns used to find rows.
Judge wrapping by its effect on scanning and row rhythm, not by table height alone.
specific: The first three columns in r0A use nearly the minimum widths needed to keep their longest unbreakable content intact.
The notes column must absorb substantial wrapping within the phone viewport.

tradeoffs: r0C gives the notes slightly more room, shortening the second data row, but its narrower speaker column wraps the header and two counts.
uncertain: The ranges are conservative point estimates: the supplied renders do not establish which nearby widths retain the same line breaks and visual quality. A designer could accept r0C if the shorter second data row is valued more than an uninterrupted speaker column.

critique.good: The paired language names, speaker counts and all headers remain intact. Rows read clearly, and the notes wrap without splitting words.
critique.problems: The notes make the first two data rows tall, leaving white space in the shorter cells; the note column is still narrow for continuous reading.
critique.cause: The first three columns use the minimum widths needed to keep their longest unbreakable content intact, leaving 142px for notes. Within the width limit, the note column cannot be widened without compromising another column.

critique.good: The wider note column gives the Bengali note a more compact shape and reduces the height of that row.
critique.problems: Two headers wrap and language names split across lines, weakening the pairing of the two scripts. The taller header offsets the saving in the body.
critique.cause: Widths of 62px and 56px leave too little text space in the name columns; 82px also leaves too little for the speaker-count header.

critique.good: The language names remain intact, and the slightly wider note column shortens the Bengali note row.
critique.problems: The speaker-count header and two counts wrap, making the numeric column harder to scan and increasing both header and final-row height.
critique.cause: The 75px speaker-count column leaves only 54px for text, below the 68px needed for its longest unbreakable content.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r0A.why: The short language and speaker columns remain intact, and the notes have enough room to read in coherent lines. The first note wraps more than in D.

r0B.why: The first and third headers and several language names break across lines, weakening the table’s hierarchy and making short labels harder to scan.

ref_equal.why: The language columns take space from the notes, leaving the last column so narrow that words break and the first two rows become excessively tall.

ref_auto.why: Headers, language names and speaker counts stay intact, while the notes have enough width for comfortable reading. The columns and rows feel well balanced.

r0C.why: The notes have useful space, but the speaker header and some counts wrap, making comparisons down that column less immediate.

raw.unsure: The screenshots are small, so some individual line breaks are difficult to distinguish.

r0B.why: The first two headers and several language names break across lines, while the notes still need substantial wrapping. The broken labels make rows harder to scan.

ref_equal.why: The note column is so narrow that words break into fragments and the first two rows become very tall. Much of the width is tied up in short language labels.

r0C.why: The language names stay intact and the notes have useful width, but the population header and two population values wrap, making comparisons less immediate.

r0A.why: Headers, language names and population values stay on one line, and the notes wrap legibly. The Bengali note takes an extra line compared with E.

ref_auto.why: Headers and short values stay intact, while the note column has enough width for a compact, readable wrap. The columns support both row reading and population comparisons.

raw.unsure: D and E are close; the judgment rests mainly on E giving the notes slightly more room without breaking the population values.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
